title: Admittance Loom — policy compiler for staged model introductions
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a policy compiler and runtime contract we call 'Admittance Loom' to turn high-level staged-introduction intent (traffic splits, step schedules, metric gates, shadow probes) into validated rollout plans and runtime policy bundles. The compiler accepts a small declarative DSL (targets, cohorts, step shapes, metric gates, rollback policies, fallback variants) and emits: 1) a human-readable rollout preview for Console, 2) a compact runtime manifest for the serving control plane, and 3) a simulator-friendly plan used for canary safety validation. Goals: make safe rollouts simple for PM/SEs, enable deterministic simulation of failure modes, keep runtime enforcement lightweight, and enable automatic rollback when guardrails are breached. Out of scope for this ticket: full UI surface polish and RBAC integration (follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: DSL v1 supports: step percentage, duration, linear/ramp/pulse shapes, cohort targeting, shadow_probe flag, metric gates (latency_ms, p95_latency, error_rate), and rollback policy by threshold/time-window.
Compiler validates plans against SLO rules and returns clear errors for incompatible mixtures (e.g., shadow_probe with immediate 100% rollouts).
Runtime manifest size <= 4KB per rollout and deserializes in <5ms in the control plane.
Console shows rollout preview with simulated telemetry and predicted exposure curve.
E2E test that triggers auto-rollback when p95_latency > 800ms for a sustained 2-minute window.
Documentation (Confluence doc + example YAML templates) published and linked from Console help.
Integration smoke with Canary Simulator dashboard (grafana link) and a GitHub PR that wires compiler into the rollout API.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly expressive DSL becomes hard to validate. Mitigation: keep v1 intentionally small, add extension points rather than features.
Risk: Runtime manifest bloat. Mitigation: compile to compact tokens and reference common templates stored server-side.
Risk: False positive rollbacks due to noisy telemetry. Mitigation: require sustained violation windows and use rolling-window aggregation with outlier clipping.
Risk: UX confusion around shadow probes vs live traffic. Mitigation: clear Console copy and example templates; default shadow_probes off for automated canaries.
